req.title: Delete only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to delete a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that a non-author user attempting to delete a post must receive HTTP 403. Three test cases are designed: (1) Positive — the actual author deletes their own post and receives HTTP 302 redirect (success path, EP); (2) Negative — a different logged-in user attempts to delete a post they did not author and receives HTTP 403 (NEG + DT); (3) Boundary — the exact post id boundary (id=1, the only seeded post) is used by a non-author, confirming 403 is returned for that specific id and not a 404 or 200 (BVA). Each test is self-contained, uses the in-process Flask test client, seeds the DB from scratch, and asserts exact status codes to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_author_can_delete_own_post
preconditions: Database is initialised with seeded data (user id=1 'test', post id=1 authored by user id=1)
expected: Status code is exactly 302, not 403 or 200
trace: R-FLASKR-020: success path — author deletes own post
blog.delete calls get_post(id, check_author=True); author_id==g.user['id'] so no abort(403)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_author_can_delete_own_post():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_author_can_delete_own_post()

tests.name: test_non_author_delete_boundary_post_id_1
preconditions: Database is initialised with seeded data; post id=1 is the only post and is authored by user id=1
User 'other' (id=2) is logged in — this is the minimum non-author id boundary
actions: POST /1/delete (id=1, the exact seeded boundary post id)
expected: HTTP 403 Forbidden for the exact boundary post id=1
Status code is exactly 403 — not 404 (post exists) and not 302 (not deleted)
trace: R-FLASKR-020: boundary — smallest valid post id used by non-author
BVA: id=1 is the minimum seeded post id; confirms 403 is returned rather than 404 or success
Catches mutations that swap abort(403) with abort(404) or remove the author check
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_non_author_delete_boundary_post_id_1():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'other', 'password': 'other'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    # Boundary: post id=1 exists (not 404) but user 'other' is not the author
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 403
    # Confirm post still exists (was not deleted)
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        post = get_db().execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
        assert post is not None
        assert post['id'] == 1

test_non_author_delete_boundary_post_id_1()

tests.name: test_unauthenticated_delete_redirects_not_403
preconditions: Database is initialised with seeded data
No user is logged in (anonymous session)
expected: HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login (login_required decorator fires before author check)
Status code is exactly 302, not 403 — distinguishes unauthenticated from unauthorised
trace: R-FLASKR-020: decision table — unauthenticated user hits login_required before get_post author check
DT: two conditions — authenticated(F) -> redirect 302; authenticated(T) + is_author(F) -> 403
Catches mutations that remove login_required or swap redirect with abort

tests.name: test_non_author_delete_nonexistent_post_returns_404
preconditions: Database is initialised with seeded data; only post id=1 exists
actions: POST /2/delete (id=2 does not exist — one beyond the seeded boundary)
expected: HTTP 404 Not Found (post does not exist, abort(404) fires before author check)
Status code is exactly 404, not 403 — confirms 403 is only for existing posts with wrong author
trace: R-FLASKR-020: boundary — id=2 is one beyond the only seeded post id=1
BVA: boundary+1 of seeded post ids; get_post aborts 404 before reaching author check
Catches mutations that swap abort(404) with abort(403) or skip the existence check
